concept.name: Exchange
concept.definition: An organized, regulated marketplace that provides a centralized facility for trading standardized instruments under a published rulebook covering membership, listing, order matching, surveillance, and clearing. The CFTC defines a board of trade as any organized exchange or other trading facility for the trading of futures, swap, and/or option contracts (7 USC 1a(6)).
concept.intuition: A regulated bazaar: everyone agrees to the same rulebook, and the venue matches buyers with sellers under surveillance.
concept.mechanics: Members submit orders to a central matching engine or auction; the exchange disseminates quotes and trade reports, enforces listing and conduct rules, and typically routes executed trades to an affiliated or designated clearinghouse.
concept.failure_modes: Technology outages, erroneous order flow, or manipulation can disrupt the single venue many participants rely on; concentration of trading also makes the exchange a potential single point of failure.
concept.misconceptions: An exchange does not set prices and does not take the other side of trades; it operates the matching mechanism and enforces the rules under which participants trade with each other.
concept.example: The New York Stock Exchange matches equity orders under its listed-company and trading rules; CME Group operates exchanges where standardized futures trade and clear through CME Clearing.
